reporting_note: No operator, authority or regulator page reached publishes event-level outage or incident reports. Incidents become public through official statements carried by the state news agency and repeated by the domestic press, so most smaller disruptions will not appear and the coverage of this record cannot be computed.

geography.note: Bahrain has 4 governorates today (Capital, Muharraq, Northern, Southern). Natural Earth draws 5, with their pre-2014 shapes, because it still includes the Central governorate that was abolished in 2014. Every record in this system is published at country level, so no governorate is ever shaded for an event. A blank map means records are not placed, not that nothing happened.

rulings.note: Capital governorate, drawn with its pre-2014 extent. The governorate is larger today (38 square km in 2012, 78 in 2015 in the official area series), so a place in today's Capital governorate may lie outside this shape.
Southern governorate, drawn as Natural Earth has it, from before the 2014 redivision; whether its extent changed then was not verified. Includes the Hawar Islands as Natural Earth draws them.

Central governorate: abolished in 2014, when the governorates were redivided into four (Survey and Land Registration Bureau, Area by Governorate). Drawn because Natural Earth still carries it; never assigned an event and never given an event count. An event that a source locates in this area is recorded at country level, not moved to a neighbouring unit.
Northern governorate, drawn as Natural Earth has it, from before the 2014 redivision; whether its extent changed then was not verified.

precision_policy.reason: Bahrain is about 780 square kilometres with a handful of energy facilities, and the map source still draws the five governorates that were replaced by four in 2014. A governorate would either identify the facility or place an event in a shape that no longer exists, so every record is the country's. Attacks and sabotage also carry no facility or operator.

refinery.basis: BH_SOURCE_AUDIT: the national refining series describes a single refinery.

lng_terminal.basis: The lead's reading of public reporting (iteration 20): one LNG import terminal. Not yet confirmed in the source audit; an entry here can only hold a record, never publish one.

sectors.reason: The official refining series describe a single refinery, so a sector score would be one facility's status under another name. Annual national throughput and output are shown as context only.

National installed capacity is published (IRENA), but the utility's station list was not read and its series covers public supply only, about half of national generation. With this few stations a governorate share would identify a station.
No inventory was read and none should be built: a substation-level picture of a grid this small is outside the scope boundary.
No public capacity inventory was read, and building one would centre on import and export routing, which is out of scope.

National production is published annually and shown as context. Processing sits with a single operating group, so a score would be that group's facility status; LNG and storage are not yet researched.
Not applicable: IRENA reports coal at 0% of Bahrain's total energy supply (2022) and no coal in power generation. The sector does not exist here, which is different from unknown.
